newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan forces attack rebels in north, east.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan forces attack rebels in north, east.

text.p: Sri Lankan armed forces, backed by aircraft and artillery, launched two offensives against Tamil Tiger rebels in the north and east on Tuesday, military officials said.
Troops of the army's elite air mobile and independent brigades were scouring the jungles of Batticaloa district, about 200 km (125 miles) east of Colombo, they said.
Other army units launched an operation in the eastern part of the northern Jaffna peninsula, 320 km (200 miles) from Colombo, they said.

"We're attacking terrorist jungle bases in the east," Sri Lanka's army chief, Lieutenant-General Rohan Daluwatte, told Reuters. "In Jaffna, we launched an operation to clear the eastern part of the peninsula."
Troops were supported by artillery and the air force while the navy patrolled offshore to prevent Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels escaping by boat, military officials said.
The offensive in eastern Batticaloa was launched after intelligence reports of a rebel build-up in the area, they said.

There were no immediate reports of fighting, but military officials said the operation in the east was centred around the Maha Oya-Chenkaladi highway, a supply route for the military, which connects Batticaloa to the interior.
The rebels usually withdraw in the face of the advancing army, military officials said.
The Tigers, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the north and east of the predominantly Sinhalese island, have stepped up attacks in the east.
Military forces are thin on the ground there after they recaptured the rebels' northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold early this year.

Two weeks ago, a Tiger suicide bomber killed one of eastern Sri Lanka's senior police commandoes in Batticaloa. The bomber rammed his motorcycle into the jeep of the deputy chief of the police Special Task Force (STF), near Karativu.
In a separate incident the same day, seven soldiers were killed in northeastern Weli Oya when soldiers bathing in an irrigation tank set off a mine laid underwater by the rebels.

The Tigers overran an STF camp at Pulukunava in Amparai district, adjoining Batticaloa, the week before, killing 36 security personnel. It was the Tigers' biggest attack on government forces in more than two months.
The military launched an offensive against guerrilla jungle bases shortly after that attack, but the rebels abandoned their camps and withdrew without a fight.
The STF then withdrew from at least four of their camps, raising fears among Sinhalese villagers in the area that they might be vulnerable to rebel assaults.
The military's eastern commanders have repeatedly complained they were short of troops to dominate the region after several bases were closed and troops redeployed to the north to capture Jaffna.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
